title: Purely inseparable integral extensions have a unique prime over each prime
statement: Let $A\subseteq B$ be a finite integral extension of domains, assume that $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let the fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ form a finite purely inseparable extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ there is exactly one prime ideal of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, proof, sentence 'Since A subset B subset C are finite and L/M/K are purely inseparable ... there is a unique prime lying over p'; the integral/radicial argument is made explicit
